gap_solution: NCRYPT_PIN_PROPERTY is implemented: the PIN is handed to the session layer, and because sessions open lazily a PIN set before the first cryptographic call is the one used to log in. Token selection is read-only through this call by design — the session pool is already bound to a slot by then and PKCS#11 cannot move a session between tokens, so accepting the value would be worse than refusing it. Choose the token with SOFTHSM2_SLOT or SOFTHSM2_TOKEN_LABEL and read it back with KSP_SLOT_PROPERTY.

detail: Wrapping an external private key onto the token
gap_solution: Returns NTE_NOT_SUPPORTED. Would need C_CreateObject with private material or C_UnwrapKey. Contradicts the HSM posture; only add if a migration workflow demands it.

Import is implemented: BCRYPT_KEY_DATA_BLOB creates a CKO_SECRET_KEY via C_CreateObject with CKA_VALUE, AES for 16/24/32-byte material and a generic secret otherwise. Export is refused and will stay refused — every key this provider creates or imports is CKA_EXTRACTABLE=FALSE, which is the point of the HSM model. Making export work would mean creating extractable keys, weakening every deployment to satisfy one blob type.
Same constraint as FMT-07: it is a private-key format and keys are non-extractable.
Would let keys move between instances of the same provider. Needs a defined wrapping format; no standard to follow.

NCRYPT_MACHINE_KEY_FLAG is honoured on CreatePersistedKey, OpenKey and EnumKeys: the scope becomes a CKA_LABEL prefix ("m/name" or "u/name"), so a machine key and a user key of the same name are distinct objects instead of silently aliasing. Enumeration filters by scope and reports unprefixed names. This is NAMESPACING, NOT ISOLATION — anyone who can log into the token can read either scope. Real isolation needs an ACL model PKCS#11 does not provide within a slot, and no amount of label work supplies one.
Fundamental: SoftHSM2 is a software token using encrypted SQLite. Only fixable by pointing the KSP at a real HSM which the PKCS#11 abstraction already allows.
Follows from OPS-01. Requires certified hardware and a formal validation programme.

Handled inside vendor PKCS#11 libraries. Our KSP would inherit it automatically when pointed at such a library; nothing to implement.
